key_developments: 16 September — FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on a 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023, lifting the 2026 median from 3.8% to 4.1% and the 2027 median from 3.6% to 4.1%; DXY broke 100.00 and GBP/USD fell 97 pips to 1.33802, EUR/USD 79 pips to 1.14635, USD/CHF rose 71 pips to 0.82594.
17 September — The MPC held Bank Rate at 3.75% on a 6-3 vote with Greene, Mann and Pill dissenting and agreed to slow gilt sales; GBP/USD closed at the cycle low of 1.33579 and GBP/AUD fell 92 pips.

18 September — The BoJ raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.25% on a 7-2 vote but underwhelmed on cadence; the yen weakened as much as 0.8% to 157.145, GBP/JPY rose 178 pips to 210.14203 and USD/JPY 92 pips to 156.89522.
18 September — Japan's August core inflation slowed to 1.7% from 1.8%, and the Nikkei reported a BoJ rate check late in the session, after which the yen pared losses.
17 September — New Zealand Q2 GDP beat at +0.2% q/q and 2.6% y/y; NZD/USD moved from 0.5718 to 0.5724 and AUD/NZD rose 48 pips the following session.
16 September — UK August CPI rose to 3.1% but core CPIH held at 2.9% and services at 3.6%, so the hawkish sterling case rested on headline energy only.
new_risks_identified: The BoJ's 7-2 split, with both dissenters nominated by Prime Minister Takaichi, is a structural brake on the cadence thesis behind every yen-cross short — a risk the original analysis did not name.

Brent at $103.21 on 18 September, up 12.65% over the month after three East-West pipeline pumping stations were damaged, cuts for the Canadian dollar and against sterling, the euro and the yen simultaneously.
The 29 September RBA decision at 78-87% priced has inverted asymmetry: a hold would hit Short GBP/AUD and Long AUD/NZD together while rescuing Short AUD/USD.
UK 30-year issuance at 5.8168%, the costliest since the DMO was founded in 1998, has cut Budget headroom to roughly £13bn ahead of 28 October.
consensus_shifts: Euro-area rate forecasts revised higher: Nomura and Citi now see two more hikes to a 3.00% deposit rate, HSBC and UBS one more, and 67.0% is priced for 2.75% on 29 October — validating the EUR/GBP rates case even as spot refuses to move.

Sell-side moved against the GBP/JPY cadence thesis: Morgan Stanley's Sugisaki argues the BoJ must reach 1.75-2% quickly to change the behind-the-curve perception, and NAB called the meeting clearly underwhelming.
The GBP/AUD five-provider survey is unchanged at 1.8848, still above spot, so consensus has not moved toward the short at all despite four houses validating the Australian rate case.
No pair-level revisions found for SGD/CHF, AUD/NZD or AUD/USD; the 0.71-0.73 AUD/USD sell-side band now has spot at its floor.
